questions.q: Why stage the query as a view instead of pasting it into Power BI as a native query?
options: A view is one object you can test and fix independently in SSMS, instead of a query buried in the report
Power BI cannot connect to SQL Server views
Views run automatically without a scheduled refresh
There is no real difference between the two approaches
questions.explain: A view lives in the database as a reviewable, testable object, rather than literal query text with nowhere central to fix it.

questions.q: What does dbo.vw_CarrawayWeeklySalesFact carry, per the Lesson 2 architecture?
options: Order-line keys and numbers only — TerritoryID and ProductID, not the names
Every column from all five original tables, fully joined
Only TerritoryName and ProductName, no keys
Just the SalesOrderID column
questions.explain: The fact view sticks to keys plus OrderQty/LineTotal/dates; names live only in the two dimension views.

questions.q: Why does vw_CarrawayProductDim use a LEFT JOIN to ProductSubcategory?
options: So products with a NULL ProductSubcategoryID still get a row, with SubcategoryName as NULL
Because LEFT JOIN is faster than INNER JOIN
Because ProductSubcategory has no primary key
It uses INNER JOIN, not LEFT JOIN
questions.explain: The same reasoning from Lesson 3 carries over: an inner join there would silently drop products without a subcategory.

questions.q: Why use CREATE OR ALTER VIEW instead of CREATE VIEW?
options: It updates the view in place if it already exists, instead of erroring out — useful since Lesson 15 modifies this view again
CREATE VIEW is deprecated in SQL Server
CREATE OR ALTER VIEW runs faster
There is no functional difference
questions.explain: CREATE OR ALTER lets the same script be safely re-run to update the view, which matters when Lesson 15's change request revisits it.

questions.q: What should the row count of dbo.vw_CarrawayWeeklySalesFact equal?
options: The same COUNT(*) verified in Lessons 2 and 3 for shipped order lines
The total number of rows in Production.Product
Exactly 1,000 rows
The number of territories in Sales.SalesTerritory
questions.explain: Matching the earlier verified count confirms the view's join and filter logic didn't drop or duplicate any order lines.
